title: Hysteresis autoscaler, opportunistic prewarm, and fair admission shedding for hosted GPU pools
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: After a recurring capacity event on 2025-02-17 we observed persistent queue buildup and client-visible latency spikes across hosted GPU pools when long-sequence workloads surged. Root causes: (1) autoscaler hysteresis and cooldown parameters caused slow scale-up for sustained bursts, (2) cold-starts for large models amplified queueing, (3) admission controller lacked priority-aware shedding and fairness for reserved vs best-effort traffic. Goal: deliver a set of coordinated fixes that reduce tail queue time by 70%, eliminate class-wide 5xx spikes for priority customers, and restore steady-state autoscale responsiveness without oscillation. Proposed changes: implement hysteresis-aware autoscaler (rate-limited scale-up with dynamic cooldown tuned by request mix), opportunistic prewarm nodes for long-seq models using low-cost warm pools (preemptible with fast teardown), and a priority-aware admission-shedding policy that applies graceful failures to best-effort workloads while protecting reserved traffic. Success criteria: p95 queue wait time under 200ms on 99th percentile traffic days, zero customer priority 5xx events during simulated 3x burst test, and no more than a 5% increase in infra cost at target load. Observability: add new metrics (prewarm_usage_ratio, hysteresis_state, shed_rate_by_priority) and dashboards + alert thresholds. Rollout plan: dev feature flag -> canary on non-prod -> canary on 1 hosted-region with rollback window -> full rollout. Risks & mitigations: prewarm increases cost (limit to 10% of pool, cold eviction policy), admission changes risk user-facing errors (gradual ramp and canary small token buckets), autoscale tuning may oscillate (add safety cap and test harness), KV-cache priming still required (follow-up token).
